parts.text: Micah calls the earth to hear the Lord’s witness against Samaria and Jerusalem. God comes from his holy place, and mountains and valleys melt before him. Israel’s transgression centres in Samaria, while Judah’s corruption reaches Jerusalem. Samaria will become rubble, and its idols and accumulated wealth will be destroyed.

Micah mourns because the wound extends into Judah and reaches Jerusalem’s gate. He addresses a succession of towns with warnings of shame, flight, disappointment, and conquest. Their familiar places become signs of approaching distress. The chapter closes by calling for mourning over beloved children carried into captivity, bringing the national warning down to the grief of families.

chapters.title: Oppression rebuked and a remnant gathered

parts.text: God condemns those who plan evil at night and seize fields and houses when morning gives them opportunity. They rob families of their inheritance, so their own land will be divided to others. The people reject unwelcome prophecy while mistreating peaceful travellers, women, and children. They would rather hear flattering promises of drink than God’s correction.

Against these warnings, the LORD promises to gather Jacob and assemble Israel’s remnant like a great flock in its fold. The one who breaks open the way goes before them, and they pass through the gate. Their king leads them, with the LORD at their head. The closing promise presents gathering and leadership after the chapter’s exposure of dispossession and false security.

Micah confronts leaders who should know justice but instead love evil and devour the people, described through shocking images of butchery. Their future cries to God will go unanswered because of their conduct. Prophets likewise promise peace to those who feed them and hostility to those who do not. Darkness will expose their lack of an answer from God.

Micah contrasts their deception with the LORD’s Spirit empowering him to declare Israel’s sin. Rulers build with bloodshed, judges take bribes, priests teach for payment, and prophets sell divination. Yet they presume that God’s presence guarantees safety. Because of them, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem reduced to ruins, and the temple mountain overgrown.

chapters.title: Peace from Zion beyond present distress

parts.text: In the last days, the LORD’s house is exalted and nations come to learn his ways. His judgment turns weapons into farming tools and ends instruction in warfare. People dwell without fear beneath vine and fig tree. God gathers the lame, scattered, and afflicted, making them a strong remnant over whom he reigns in Zion.

Jerusalem’s present pain is compared to childbirth. The people will leave the city and go to Babylon, but there the Lord will redeem them from their enemies. Nations gathering against Zion do not understand his purpose: he gathers them like sheaves for threshing. Zion is called to rise, overcome them, and devote their gain to the Lord of the whole earth.

Amid siege and humiliation, Beth-lehem Ephratah is promised as the birthplace of a ruler in Israel whose goings forth are from everlasting. His people will return, and he will feed them in the LORD’s strength, with greatness reaching the earth’s ends. He will be their peace, and deliverance is promised when the Assyrian invades.

Jacob’s remnant among the nations is compared both to refreshing dew and to a powerful lion. Its enemies will be overcome. God will also remove the people’s misplaced securities: horses, chariots, strongholds, witchcraft, images, and groves. They will no longer worship what their own hands have made, while divine vengeance reaches the nations.

The LORD presents his case before mountains and the earth’s foundations. He asks how he has burdened Israel, reminding them of deliverance from Egypt and protection during Balak’s schemes. A questioner imagines ever greater sacrifices, even a firstborn child. The answer points to what God has already shown: do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with him.

God then addresses the city’s fraudulent measures, violence, and lies. Such practices cannot be treated as pure. The people will suffer frustrated labour: eating without satisfaction, sowing without reaping, and pressing fruit without enjoying its produce. By following Omri’s statutes and Ahab’s works, they bring desolation and reproach upon themselves.

chapters.title: Waiting for the God who pardons

parts.text: Micah laments the disappearance of upright people. Leaders demand bribes, neighbours cannot be trusted, and even households are divided. Yet he resolves to wait for the God of his salvation. Though acknowledging sin and accepting the LORD’s indignation, he trusts that God will bring him from darkness into light and silence the enemy’s taunts.

The chapter anticipates rebuilding and gathering while recognizing judgment upon the land’s wrongdoing. A prayer asks God to shepherd his people as before, and he promises wonders recalling the exodus. Nations will be humbled. The closing praise celebrates God’s unmatched willingness to pardon, delight in mercy, subdue iniquity, and fulfil the promises sworn to Abraham and Jacob.
